raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

- To continue from a cached prefix, the server needs the SWA KV of the last `sliding_window` tokens of that prefix. Older SWA KV on the same path is no longer needed.
- When the SWA pool is full, the unified cache frees SWA KV in plain LRU order. An idle conversation is the least recently used, so its last window is freed before the old windows that active conversations leave behind on every turn.
- When the idle conversation comes back, only the shared system prompt is a cache hit. The rest is prefilled again, even though its full KV is still cached.
- #35515 by @QAQEthan fixes this in `swa_radix_cache.py`, but that file is no longer on main. This PR brings the same idea to the unified cache, for both the Python core and the Rust core.

## Modifications

- A node counts as the end of a branch when a leaf or a fork lies less than one window of live SWA tokens below it. These nodes hold the windows that a later request needs.
- `_evict_device_next_node` now skips these nodes on its first pass. If it reaches the end of the LRU list and it skipped some nodes, it starts again from the oldest entry and frees them in LRU order. So eviction still succeeds wherever it succeeded before.
- The same change is made in `rust/sglang-radix-tree/src/components/swa.rs`. `ComponentState` gets two new flags to track the two passes.
- A `joint_lru` eviction walk (#46827) picks each SWA victim itself, so it turns the skipping off. Otherwise the walk would skip a picked window and free a later one. `joint_lru` only runs on the Python core.
- One difference from #35515: a window that sits above an already freed (tombstoned) node is not protected. In the unified cache almost every live window sits above one, because of chunk boundaries and older turns, so protecting them would protect everything. A window above a fork, such as the shared system prompt, is still protected.
- Two existing Rust tests expected the old eviction order and are updated.
- Cost: on the first pass, each candidate node needs a short walk down the tree, covering at most one window of tokens. When the pool only holds protected windows, each eviction scans the SWA LRU list once before it frees anything.

Related PRs that do not overlap with this one:

- #39694 limits the number of live windows per path at insert time.
- #40283 frees the slots outside the window when a request finishes.
- #40338 moves this walk into a shared base class. Whichever of that PR and this one lands second will need a small rebase.
- #42703 keeps an opt-in margin of extra SWA tokens behind the end of each insert. If it lands, the span that this PR spares should grow by that margin.
- #43009 rebuilds an evicted window on a cache hit instead of prefilling the whole suffix again. With this PR that rebuild is needed less often.

## Accuracy Tests

This PR does not change model output. It only changes which SWA KV is freed first.

Unit tests on `df8a84eddb` (with main merged in at `14ad64c411`), run in the `nightly-dev-cu13-20261009` image with the source tree on `PYTHONPATH`, on 1 GPU:

```bash
SGLANG_RUST_BUILD_MODE=auto SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=python \
  python -m pytest -q --continue-on-collection-errors test/registered/unit/mem_cache
SGLANG_RUST_BUILD_MODE=auto SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=rust \
  python -m pytest -q --continue-on-collection-errors test/registered/unit/mem_cache
cd rust/sglang-radix-tree
TORCH_ROOT=$(python3 -c 'import pathlib, torch; print(pathlib.Path(torch.__file__).parent)')
LIBTORCH_USE_PYTORCH=1 LIBTORCH_BYPASS_VERSION_CHECK=1 CXXFLAGS="-std=c++20 -include $PWD/torch_compat.h" \
  LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$TORCH_ROOT/lib" cargo test --locked
```

| suite | this PR | main `14ad64c411` |
|---|---|---|
| `unit/mem_cache`, Python core | 3367 passed, 5 failed, 6 errors | 3351 passed, 5 failed, 6 errors |
| `unit/mem_cache`, Rust core | 3367 passed, 5 failed, 6 errors | 3350 passed, 7 failed, 6 errors |
| `cargo test` | 933 passed | 930 passed |

- The failures and errors are the same on both builds: 4 tests in `test_unified_hicache_transfer_lifecycle.py` and `TestMambaCompaction::test_cuda_directions_and_move_paths` (CUDA errors in this image), and collection errors in `test_page_interleave_shard.py` and `test_umbp_store.py` (`mori` and `parameterized` are not installed).
- Main's Rust-core run also failed `test_hicache_nixl_storage.py::TestNixlUnified::test_dsa_indexer_bounce_round_trip_preserves_every_byte` once (`NIXL_ERR_BACKEND`).
- New tests: `test_swa_evict_reclaims_branch_tails_last` and `test_swa_evict_spares_the_window_above_a_fork` (16 parametrized cases, both cores), plus 3 Rust tests. The 16 Python cases fail on main `14ad64c411` with both cores.
- After merging main at `ce329c85fa`: main split `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` into topic files, so the two new tests now live in `unified_radix_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_core.py`. On `test/registered/unit/mem_cache` and `test/registered/radix_cache/unified_radix_tree` (without the two files that do not collect), this PR gives 3359 passed and main gives 3343 passed, with the same 7 failures and 90 errors on both, for both cores. `cargo test` gives 933 passed on this PR and 930 on main.
- After merging main at `4ffc9e1b7d`: `test/registered/unit/mem_cache` and `test/registered/radix_cache/unified_radix_tree` give 3568 passed, 5 failed, 102 errors on this branch and 3551 passed, 5 failed, 102 errors on main, on both cores, with the same failing tests, comparing subtest failures too. `cargo test` gives 952 passed on this branch and 949 on main. The new `test_joint_walk_evicts_a_picked_window_above_a_fork` fails without the `joint_lru` change above.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

4x B300, TP4 + EP4. I use `--max-total-tokens 400000` and `--swa-full-tokens-ratio` to make the SWA pool small, so that eviction happens in a short run. Both builds run in the `nightly-dev-cu13-20261009` image. Its `sglang-kernel` 0.4.9 has no `flash_mla_mega`, so both builds use `--dsv4-attn-backend flashmla`.

```bash
sglang serve --trust-remote-code --model-path nvidia/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-NVFP4 \
  --tp 4 --ep-size 4 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31710 \
  --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 \
  --enable-cache-report --dsv4-attn-backend flashmla --max-total-tokens 400000 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.06
```

Workload:

- 40 conversations share a 1024-token system prompt. Each has a first turn of about 4.3k tokens.
- 8 conversations are busy and send one turn every round. 32 are idle and send one turn every 8 rounds.
- 40 rounds, concurrency 4, 160 output tokens, temperature 0.
- "cached / prompt" is the share of prompt tokens served from the cache, from `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`.

This PR at `df8a84eddb`, main at `14ad64c411`:

| SWA pool (tokens) | build | busy: cached / prompt | idle: cached / prompt | idle requests that only hit the system prompt | idle TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 23,808 (ratio 0.06) | main, run 1 | 0.961 | 0.277 | 146 / 160 | 118.3 / 201.8 |
| 23,808 (ratio 0.06) | main, run 2 | 0.961 | 0.281 | 145 / 160 | 158.4 / 227.9 |
| 23,808 (ratio 0.06) | this PR, run 1 | 0.950 | 0.805 | 31 / 160 | 154.3 / 163.8 |
| 23,808 (ratio 0.06) | this PR, run 2 | 0.960 | 0.819 | 28 / 160 | 155.8 / 171.0 |
| 23,808 (ratio 0.06) | main, `--no-enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` | 0.968 | 0.297 | 142 / 160 | 184.7 / 248.3 |
| 23,808 (ratio 0.06) | this PR, `--no-enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` | 0.968 | 0.953 | 0 / 160 | 145.9 / 151.5 |
| 39,936 (ratio 0.1) | main | 0.962 | 0.935 | 2 / 160 | 145.1 / 154.5 |
| 39,936 (ratio 0.1) | this PR | 0.962 | 0.938 | 1 / 160 | 158.1 / 220.5 |

- Each row is one server launch. TTFT moves by tens of ms between runs of the same build, so the TTFT columns do not separate the builds.
- 23,808 tokens: the pool has room for the last window of every conversation, but not for the old windows as well. This is the case the PR fixes.
- 39,936 tokens: this workload never fills the pool, so both builds behave the same.
- The remaining idle misses at 23,808 tokens come from main's decoder SWA bounded replay for DeepSeek-V4.1 (#41303). It holds back one window at the end of every match, so the next turn's match can end one page above the branch end, outside the spared window. With `--no-enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` this PR has 0 / 160 misses. Sparing that page as well, by keeping two windows per branch, was worse at this pool size (idle cached / prompt of 0.516 and 0.447 in two runs), so this PR does not do it.
- At 9,984 tokens (ratio 0.025), main `14ad64c411` stopped making progress in round 37, so that pool size is not re-measured. At `6697607914`, both builds lost the cache in the same way at that size (idle cached / prompt 0.219 on main, 0.218 with this PR).

<details><summary>Workload script</summary>

```python
"""Multi-turn agent workload against a live server: a few busy conversations, many parked in tool calls.

usage: bench.py <base_url> <out.json>
Each turn appends the model's reply and a short tool result, then asks again. Reports cached prompt
tokens (server usage) and TTFT per request, split by busy / parked conversations.
"""
import json
import random
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

URL, OUT = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
N_BUSY, N_PARKED, PARK_EVERY, ROUNDS, CONC = 8, 32, 8, 40, 4
WORDS = open("/usr/share/dict/words").read().split() if False else None
VOCAB = ["alpha", "bravo", "charlie", "delta", "echo", "foxtrot", "golf", "hotel", "india", "juliet", "kilo", "lima",
         "mike", "november", "oscar", "papa", "quebec", "romeo", "sierra", "tango", "uniform", "victor", "whiskey",
         "xray", "yankee", "zulu", "river", "stone", "cloud", "engine", "ledger", "packet", "socket", "tensor",
         "kernel", "window", "branch", "cursor", "budget", "signal"]


def words(rng, n):
    return " ".join(rng.choice(VOCAB) for _ in range(n))


SYSTEM = "You are a terse operations agent. Rules:\n" + "\n".join(
    f"{i}. {words(random.Random(i), 18)}." for i in range(40)
)
MODEL = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f"{URL}/v1/models"))["data"][0]["id"]


def ask(messages):
    body = {"model": MODEL, "messages": messages, "max_tokens": 160, "temperature": 0, "stream": True,
            "stream_options": {"include_usage": True}, "chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking": False}}
    req = urllib.request.Request(f"{URL}/v1/chat/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    t0, ttft, text, usage = time.perf_counter(), None, [], None
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=900) as r:
        for line in r:
            if not line.startswith(b"data: ") or line.strip() == b"data: [DONE]":
                continue
            ev = json.loads(line[6:])
            if ev.get("usage"):
                usage = ev["usage"]
            for ch in ev.get("choices", []):
                d = ch.get("delta", {})
                piece = d.get("content") or d.get("reasoning_content")
                if piece:
                    ttft = ttft or time.perf_counter() - t0
                    text.append(piece)
    return "".join(text), usage, ttft


class Conv:
    def __init__(self, cid):
        self.cid, self.rng, self.turn = cid, random.Random(1000 + cid), 0
        self.kind = "busy" if cid < N_BUSY else "parked"
        doc = words(self.rng, 2200)
        self.messages = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM},
                         {"role": "user", "content": f"Incident {cid} log:\n{doc}\n\nSummarize the next action in two sentences."}]

    def step(self, rnd):
        text, usage, ttft = ask(self.messages)
        cached = ((usage.get("prompt_tokens_details") or {}).get("cached_tokens")) or 0
        row = {"conv": self.cid, "kind": self.kind, "round": rnd, "turn": self.turn, "prompt": usage["prompt_tokens"],
               "cached": cached, "ttft": ttft}
        self.messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": text or "ok"})
        self.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": f"Tool result {self.turn}: {words(self.rng, 50)}. Continue."})
        self.turn += 1
        return row


convs = [Conv(c) for c in range(N_BUSY + N_PARKED)]
rows = []
with ThreadPoolExecutor(CONC) as pool:
    # Round -1: cold start, one conversation at a time so cold prefills do not fight over the SWA pool.
    rows += [c.step(-1) for c in convs]
    for rnd in range(ROUNDS):
        due = [c for c in convs if c.kind == "busy" or (c.cid % PARK_EVERY) == rnd % PARK_EVERY]
        rows += pool.map(lambda c, rnd=rnd: c.step(rnd), due)
        print(f"round {rnd} done", flush=True)
json.dump(rows, open(OUT, "w"))
```

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

nodes.body: @hzh0425 @ispobock could one of you take a look and add `run-ci` when you have time? It changes the order of SWA eviction in the unified radix cache so a branch's last window goes last. I merged main today and re-ran the tests and the idle-conversation benchmark. One open question is in the description: with DeepSeek-V4.1 bounded replay on by default (#41303), matches can end one page above the protected window, so some misses come back. I would like your view on whether to handle that here or in a follow-up.

[by Claude Code]

We measured this PR on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash under AgentX: TP4, the InferenceX GB200 agentic recipe, page 256, DSpark,
900 s windows. It fixes the idle-conversation miss, but at agentic load it also makes
short-gap turns miss more often. A small addition, sparing the window that a running request's prompt-end checkpoint
builds, removes that and matches a 4x larger SWA pool.

**Which window the next turn needs.** AgentX replays recorded traces, so a follow-up prompt is the previous prompt plus
the recorded assistant message plus the tool result, never the model's own output. Reuse therefore lands at the
previous **prompt end**: in our trace replays, most follow-ups land exactly there, and none land inside the
previous output. The same happens in real serving whenever the client re-renders history differently from the generated tokens.

**Results.** End-to-end numbers will be posted on #45430.

**Why this PR alone misses more at short gaps.** Between turns, the previous prompt-end window has one child (the
generated output) and sits more than a window above it, so `_is_in_branch_tail` does not spare it. The output-end leaf
is spared, though no follow-up ever matches it. The first pass therefore evicts recent prompt-end windows before old
spared leaves. Most of the extra misses are one-turn lags.

**Addition.**
- The post-prefill checkpoint marks the window it inserts when the request is not finished and the page-aligned insert
  ends at the page-aligned prompt end. If that window already exists, for example because the last chunk was under a
  page, the checkpoint marks the existing node instead.
- The first pass spares marked nodes the same way it spares branch tails. A split copies the bit, and a tombstone
  clears it.
- In both cores this is about 60 lines plus tests, behind `SGLANG_OPT_SWA_PROTECT_PROMPT_TAIL` (default off).

We opened it as #45430, stacked on this branch (one commit on top of `9a64a740e1`). If you would rather fold it into
this PR, we are happy to do that instead; otherwise we will rebase #45430 onto main once this lands.

I merged main at `4ffc9e1b7d` and it merges cleanly again. #46827 added the `joint_lru` eviction policy in the same SWA walk, so a joint walk now turns the tail skipping off, and a new test covers that. The description has the new unit test and `cargo test` numbers.

@hzh0425 @ispobock could one of you take a look and add `run-ci` when you have time?

| SWA pool (tokens) | build | busy: cached / prompt | idle: cached / prompt | idle requests that only hit the system prompt | idle TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 23,808 (ratio 0.06) | main, run 1 | 0.961 | 0.277 | 146 / 160 | 118.3 / 201.8 |
| 23,808 (ratio 0.06) | main, run 2 | 0.961 | 0.281 | 145 / 160 | 158.4 / 227.9 |
| 23,808 (ratio 0.06) | this PR, run 1 | 0.950 | 0.805 | 31 / 160 | 154.3 / 163.8 |
| 23,808 (ratio 0.06) | this PR, run 2 | 0.960 | 0.819 | 28 / 160 | 155.8 / 171.0 |
| 23,808 (ratio 0.06) | main, `--no-enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` | 0.968 | 0.297 | 142 / 160 | 184.7 / 248.3 |
| 23,808 (ratio 0.06) | this PR, `--no-enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` | 0.968 | 0.953 | 0 / 160 | 145.9 / 151.5 |
| 39,936 (ratio 0.1) | main | 0.962 | 0.935 | 2 / 160 | 145.1 / 154.5 |
| 39,936 (ratio 0.1) | this PR | 0.962 | 0.938 | 1 / 160 | 158.1 / 220.5 |

- Each row is one server launch. TTFT moves by tens of ms between runs of the same build, so the TTFT columns do not separate the builds.
- 23,808 tokens: the pool has room for the last window of every conversation, but not for the old windows as well. This is the case the PR fixes.
- 39,936 tokens: this workload never fills the pool, so both builds behave the same.
- The remaining idle misses at 23,808 tokens come from main's decoder SWA bounded replay for DeepSeek-V4.1 (#41303). It holds back one window at the end of every match, so the next turn's match can end one page above the branch end, outside the spared window. With `--no-enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` this PR has 0 / 160 misses. Sparing that page as well, by keeping two windows per branch, was worse at this pool size (idle cached / prompt of 0.516 and 0.447 in two runs), so this PR does not do it.
- At 9,984 tokens (ratio 0.025), main `14ad64c411` stopped making progress in round 37, so that pool size is not re-measured. At `6697607914`, both builds lost the cache in the same way at that size (idle cached / prompt 0.219 on main, 0.218 with this PR).

<details><summary>Workload script</summary>

```python
"""Multi-turn agent workload against a live server: a few busy conversations, many parked in tool calls.

usage: bench.py <base_url> <out.json>
Each turn appends the model's reply and a short tool result, then asks again. Reports cached prompt
tokens (server usage) and TTFT per request, split by busy / parked conversations.
"""
import json
import random
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

URL, OUT = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
N_BUSY, N_PARKED, PARK_EVERY, ROUNDS, CONC = 8, 32, 8, 40, 4
WORDS = open("/usr/share/dict/words").read().split() if False else None
VOCAB = ["alpha", "bravo", "charlie", "delta", "echo", "foxtrot", "golf", "hotel", "india", "juliet", "kilo", "lima",
         "mike", "november", "oscar", "papa", "quebec", "romeo", "sierra", "tango", "uniform", "victor", "whiskey",
         "xray", "yankee", "zulu", "river", "stone", "cloud", "engine", "ledger", "packet", "socket", "tensor",
         "kernel", "window", "branch", "cursor", "budget", "signal"]


def words(rng, n):
    return " ".join(rng.choice(VOCAB) for _ in range(n))


SYSTEM = "You are a terse operations agent. Rules:\n" + "\n".join(
    f"{i}. {words(random.Random(i), 18)}." for i in range(40)
)
MODEL = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f"{URL}/v1/models"))["data"][0]["id"]


def ask(messages):
    body = {"model": MODEL, "messages": messages, "max_tokens": 160, "temperature": 0, "stream": True,
            "stream_options": {"include_usage": True}, "chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking": False}}
    req = urllib.request.Request(f"{URL}/v1/chat/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    t0, ttft, text, usage = time.perf_counter(), None, [], None
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=900) as r:
        for line in r:
            if not line.startswith(b"data: ") or line.strip() == b"data: [DONE]":
                continue
            ev = json.loads(line[6:])
            if ev.get("usage"):
                usage = ev["usage"]
            for ch in ev.get("choices", []):
                d = ch.get("delta", {})
                piece = d.get("content") or d.get("reasoning_content")
                if piece:
                    ttft = ttft or time.perf_counter() - t0
                    text.append(piece)
    return "".join(text), usage, ttft


class Conv:
    def __init__(self, cid):
        self.cid, self.rng, self.turn = cid, random.Random(1000 + cid), 0
        self.kind = "busy" if cid < N_BUSY else "parked"
        doc = words(self.rng, 2200)
        self.messages = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM},
                         {"role": "user", "content": f"Incident {cid} log:\n{doc}\n\nSummarize the next action in two sentences."}]

    def step(self, rnd):
        text, usage, ttft = ask(self.messages)
        cached = ((usage.get("prompt_tokens_details") or {}).get("cached_tokens")) or 0
        row = {"conv": self.cid, "kind": self.kind, "round": rnd, "turn": self.turn, "prompt": usage["prompt_tokens"],
               "cached": cached, "ttft": ttft}
        self.messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": text or "ok"})
        self.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": f"Tool result {self.turn}: {words(self.rng, 50)}. Continue."})
        self.turn += 1
        return row


convs = [Conv(c) for c in range(N_BUSY + N_PARKED)]
rows = []
with ThreadPoolExecutor(CONC) as pool:
    # Round -1: cold start, one conversation at a time so cold prefills do not fight over the SWA pool.
    rows += [c.step(-1) for c in convs]
    for rnd in range(ROUNDS):
        due = [c for c in convs if c.kind == "busy" or (c.cid % PARK_EVERY) == rnd % PARK_EVERY]
        rows += pool.map(lambda c, rnd=rnd: c.step(rnd), due)
        print(f"round {rnd} done", flush=True)
json.dump(rows, open(OUT, "w"))
```

issue_comments.body: @hzh0425 @ispobock could one of you take a look and add `run-ci` when you have time? It changes the order of SWA eviction in the unified radix cache so a branch's last window goes last. I merged main today and re-ran the tests and the idle-conversation benchmark. One open question is in the description: with DeepSeek-V4.1 bounded replay on by default (#41303), matches can end one page above the protected window, so some misses come back. I would like your view on whether to handle that here or in a follow-up.

[by Claude Code]

We measured this PR on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash under AgentX: TP4, the InferenceX GB200 agentic recipe, page 256, DSpark,
900 s windows. It fixes the idle-conversation miss, but at agentic load it also makes
short-gap turns miss more often. A small addition, sparing the window that a running request's prompt-end checkpoint
builds, removes that and matches a 4x larger SWA pool.

**Which window the next turn needs.** AgentX replays recorded traces, so a follow-up prompt is the previous prompt plus
the recorded assistant message plus the tool result, never the model's own output. Reuse therefore lands at the
previous **prompt end**: in our trace replays, most follow-ups land exactly there, and none land inside the
previous output. The same happens in real serving whenever the client re-renders history differently from the generated tokens.

**Results.** End-to-end numbers will be posted on #45430.

**Why this PR alone misses more at short gaps.** Between turns, the previous prompt-end window has one child (the
generated output) and sits more than a window above it, so `_is_in_branch_tail` does not spare it. The output-end leaf
is spared, though no follow-up ever matches it. The first pass therefore evicts recent prompt-end windows before old
spared leaves. Most of the extra misses are one-turn lags.

**Addition.**
- The post-prefill checkpoint marks the window it inserts when the request is not finished and the page-aligned insert
  ends at the page-aligned prompt end. If that window already exists, for example because the last chunk was under a
  page, the checkpoint marks the existing node instead.
- The first pass spares marked nodes the same way it spares branch tails. A split copies the bit, and a tombstone
  clears it.
- In both cores this is about 60 lines plus tests, behind `SGLANG_OPT_SWA_PROTECT_PROMPT_TAIL` (default off).

We opened it as #45430, stacked on this branch (one commit on top of `9a64a740e1`). If you would rather fold it into
this PR, we are happy to do that instead; otherwise we will rebase #45430 onto main once this lands.

I merged main at `4ffc9e1b7d` and it merges cleanly again. #46827 added the `joint_lru` eviction policy in the same SWA walk, so a joint walk now turns the tail skipping off, and a new test covers that. The description has the new unit test and `cargo test` numbers.

@hzh0425 @ispobock could one of you take a look and add `run-ci` when you have time?
